questions.stem: A client of childbearing potential taking valproate asks why pregnancy planning is important. Which explanation is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Valproate can cause fetal neural tube defects and lower offspring IQ; effective contraception and pregnancy counseling are important during treatment.","B":"Valproate fetal risk is concentrated late in pregnancy, so exposure around conception carries little concern for neural-tube or structural malformations.","C":"Folic acid supplementation is sufficient to remove the medication-related neural-tube risk, so valproate can be used without additional pregnancy counseling.","D":"Valproate may cause minor reversible neonatal effects, but current labeling does not associate in-utero exposure with cognitive or structural harm."}}
questions.rationale: Valproate exposure in pregnancy is associated with major congenital malformations including neural tube defects and with decreased IQ and neurodevelopmental disorders. Option A is correct and appropriately emphasizes contraception and pregnancy counseling. Option B incorrectly shifts risk away from conception and early pregnancy. Option C overstates folic acid as eliminating medication-related risk. Option D incorrectly minimizes structural and cognitive risks.
questions.source_detail: Current divalproex labeling revised in 2026 warns of fetal congenital malformations including neural tube defects, decreased IQ, and neurodevelopmental disorders and advises effective contraception for women of childbearing potential when treatment is necessary.

questions.stem: A client taking lisinopril reports a newly confirmed pregnancy. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue lisinopril into the second trimester because the most important fetal toxicity occurs later and early pregnancy exposure does not require prompt review.","B":"Notify the prescriber promptly; when pregnancy is detected, lisinopril should be discontinued as soon as possible and treatment should be reassessed today.","C":"Continue lisinopril if blood pressure is controlled because stable maternal pressure prevents the fetal renal effects associated with this medication class.","D":"Reduce the lisinopril dose and continue it through pregnancy because lower exposure removes the fetal toxicity associated with renin-angiotensin blockade."}}
questions.rationale: Lisinopril carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity, and current labeling says to discontinue it as soon as pregnancy is detected and reassess therapy. Option B is correct. Option A delays review despite confirmed pregnancy. Option C incorrectly assumes controlled maternal blood pressure eliminates fetal toxicity. Option D incorrectly assumes dose reduction removes the risk of renin-angiotensin system blockade.
questions.source_detail: Current lisinopril labeling updated in 2026 carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity and directs clinicians to discontinue lisinopril as soon as pregnancy is detected because renin-angiotensin system drugs can injure or kill the developing fetus.

questions.stem: Soon after labor epidural placement, the fetal heart tracing develops late decelerations. Which maternal assessment should the nurse prioritize?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Assess maternal blood pressure because epidural anesthesia can cause hypotension, reduce uteroplacental perfusion, and contribute to fetal decelerations.","B":"Assess maternal temperature because acute fever is the characteristic immediate hemodynamic effect of epidural anesthesia that explains fetal decelerations.","C":"Assess maternal glucose because epidural anesthesia commonly causes abrupt hyperglycemia that directly reduces uteroplacental perfusion after placement.","D":"Assess for maternal hypertension because epidural anesthesia typically increases systemic vascular resistance enough to produce fetal decelerations."}}
questions.rationale: Epidural anesthesia can cause maternal hypotension, which can reduce uteroplacental perfusion and contribute to fetal late decelerations. Option A is correct and prioritizes blood-pressure assessment. Option B incorrectly identifies fever as the characteristic immediate hemodynamic effect. Option C incorrectly prioritizes hyperglycemia. Option D reverses the usual hemodynamic concern by expecting hypertension.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf / Open RN — Nursing Health Promotion: Labor & Delivery Care
questions.source_detail: Open RN Nursing Health Promotion (2025) identifies maternal hypotension as a cause requiring correction when late decelerations reflect uteroplacental insufficiency; epidural anesthesia is a recognized cause of maternal hypotension requiring blood-pressure and fetal monitoring.

questions.stem: A client receiving a high-dose sodium nitroprusside infusion develops unexplained metabolic acidosis, confusion, and clinical deterioration. Which toxicity should the nurse suspect?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Suspect cyanide toxicity because nitroprusside can generate cyanide faster than the body can eliminate it at higher infusion rates or sufficient exposure.","B":"Suspect thiocyanate toxicity as the immediate high-rate effect because cyanide generation remains below detoxification capacity even at higher infusion rates.","C":"Suspect methemoglobinemia as the primary early high-rate toxicity because clinically important cyanide accumulation is not associated with nitroprusside.","D":"Suspect rebound hypertension from the infusion because nitroprusside generally raises vascular resistance when administered at higher infusion rates."}}
questions.rationale: Sodium nitroprusside metabolism generates cyanide, and higher infusion rates or sufficient exposure can exceed the body's detoxification capacity. Option A is correct, especially with metabolic acidosis, confusion, and deterioration. Option B confuses acute cyanide risk with thiocyanate toxicity, which is a separate metabolite concern. Option C incorrectly makes methemoglobinemia the primary high-rate toxicity. Option D incorrectly describes rebound hypertension as the toxicity pattern.
questions.source_name: DailyMed / FDA Label — Sodium Nitroprusside Injection
questions.source_detail: DailyMed labeling updated November 17, 2025 warns that sodium nitroprusside generates dose-related cyanide that can become toxic or lethal; cyanide toxicity can present with metabolic acidosis, confusion, and clinical deterioration.

questions.stem: A client taking isotretinoin reports new depressive symptoms and a marked mood change. Which instruction is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Attribute the mood change to acne-related stress first and delay medication review unless more severe psychiatric symptoms develop during treatment.","B":"Stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber about the new mood symptoms because current labeling warns about depression and other psychiatric disorders.","C":"Reassure the client and continue routine follow-up because new depressive symptoms during isotretinoin treatment rarely require prompt evaluation.","D":"Schedule discussion at the next routine visit rather than reporting the mood change promptly because psychiatric assessment can wait until symptoms persist longer."}}
questions.rationale: Current isotretinoin labeling warns about depression, mood disturbance, psychosis, suicidality, and aggressive behavior. Option B is correct because new depressive symptoms should prompt immediate discontinuation of isotretinoin and prompt contact with the prescriber; further evaluation may be needed. Option A delays medication review. Option C minimizes a labeled psychiatric warning. Option D postpones assessment until a later visit despite new symptoms.
questions.source_detail: Isotretinoin prescribing information revised July 2026 warns about depression and other psychiatric disorders and instructs patients who develop depression or mood disturbance to stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber; further evaluation may be necessary.
